FIB_PLUS	<p>800d_7338</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #3e6c16;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3e6c16;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6c16;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006882;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006882;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006882;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mnt, +++, mnt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>cdff_bfa0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #606300;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cnw, +++, cnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>ff46_2a75</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d5d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893b80;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cek, +++, cek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3836;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d5d;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #5846c2;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hwx, +++, hwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>b7d8_f101</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene W</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mwy, +++, mwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9b3836;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #01703f;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #01703f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #01703f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, pwy, +++, pwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>61f2_fe8a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91451a;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #91451a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91451a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3e6c16;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3e6c16;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3e6c16;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #5846c2;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>b5d5_e99d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d5d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #365aa8;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #01703f;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #01703f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #01703f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>fb33_c850</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #606300;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #365aa8;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>7ec4_10c6</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b70;">Gene M</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b70;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b70;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7a3aa8;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7a3aa8;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a3aa8;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dmw, +++, dmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9b3836;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b70;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006b70;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b70;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5846c2;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ahk, +++, ahk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #91451a;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #91451a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #91451a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006882;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006882;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006882;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7a3aa8;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7a3aa8;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7a3aa8;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dfm, +++, dfm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a00;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #745a00;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a00;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006b70;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006b70;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006b70;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #5846c2;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #5846c2;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9b3836;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9b3836;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #01703f;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #01703f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #01703f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #7a3aa8;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #7a3aa8;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006d5d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #365aa8;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>d541_8701</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a00;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #745a00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006882;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006882;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006882;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene K</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893b80;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cek, +++, cek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. FIB_PLUS	<p>c4fb_af20</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #01703f;">Gene J</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #01703f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #01703f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene T</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #365aa8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #365aa8;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>b3d5_56fc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #745a00;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #745a00;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #745a00;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006882;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006882;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006882;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #815214;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #815214;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d5d;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d5d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>0b0b_7877</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #606300;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #606300;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #9d2d5d;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9d2d5d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. FIB_PLUS	<p>0412_e5c1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the order of three genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #606300;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #606300;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #606300;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #0f6497;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #0f6497;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #893b80;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #893b80;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fry, +++, fry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
